newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica's black-led ANC to recruit white Afrikaners.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica's black-led ANC to recruit white Afrikaners.

text.p: South Africa's ruling African National Congress, once reviled by whites as an army of black communist revolutionaries, said on Monday it planned to recruit white Afrikaners into its fold.
President Nelson Mandela's ANC, which ousted white supremacy in 1994 when it was swept into power with nearly two-thirds of the vote, said whites were now less hostile to blacks in government.

"A growing number of people within the white community -- including white Afrikaners -- have lost many of the prejudices they had about the ANC prior to the elections," acting ANC secretary general Cheryl Carolus told a news conference.
"This is a constituency which we need to take full account of and we need to obviously look into how we target that community and mobilise them even further for the transformation project," she said.

The ANC hopes whites, who still traditionally support the National Party of former president F.W. de Klerk or other white-led parties, will help the country's first black majority government tackle apartheid's iniquitous legacy.

But Carolus said briefings to the party's executive at a weekend strategy session had revealed that the ANC needed to make up ground among the country's poorest, particularly in mixed-race coloured and Indian communities.
"Amongst poor working class people (in the minority race groups) there is still a lot of uncertainty about the African National Congress.

"It is a matter which concerns us not only because of the votes, because it's a small percentage of votes relative to the majority of our people, but we are concerned because we believe that poor people ought to find a home in the ANC," she said.
The ANC's main support base derives from the black working class and unemployed population, those in rural areas and a solid section of black, Indian and mixed-race intellectuals.
